title: Integrating building information modeling (BIM) and LEED system at the conceptual design stage of sustainable buildings
abstract: Designing environmentally friendly buildings that provide both high performance and cost savings is of increasing interest in the development of sustainable cities. Today, we are looking at not just buildings' certification but sustainable practices that go beyond ratings to satisfy our social responsibilities. The construction industry in general will benefit from an integrated tool that will help optimize the selection process of materials, equipments, and systems at every stage of a proposed building's life. Building information modeling (BIM) has the potential to aid designers to select the right type of materials during the early design stage and to make vital decisions that have great impacts on the life cycle of sustainable buildings. This paper describes a methodology that integrates BIM with the Canadian green building certification system (LEED). Also, it explains how this integration would assist project teams in making sustaina-bility related decisions while accumulating the required number of points based on the applied green building rating system. The methodology depicts the implementation of a model that automatically cal-culates the compiled number of LEED certification points and related registration costs for green and certified materials used in designing sustainable buildings all within the concepts of BIM. Using BIM in this methodology will help designers to invent and animate sustainable buildings in 3D mode easily and efficiently at the conceptual stage. The design information of the proposed sustainable building will be produced in a timely manner by using new plug-ins, which are developed for that reason, and which will link the BIM model with an external database that stores sustainable materials and assembly groups. A real case project is presented to illustrate the usefulness and capabilities of the proposed model.
research_question: To develop and validate a methodology that integrates Building Information Modeling (BIM) with the Canadian green building certification system (LEED) to assist project teams in making sustainability-related decisions and automatically calculating LEED certification points and associated registration costs at the conceptual design stage.
study_design: Methodology development and case study application.
setting: Conceptual design stage of sustainable buildings.

participants.demographics: Not applicable; the study focuses on a methodological tool for designers, not human participants in an experiment.

environmental_features.details: A software plug-in for Autodesk Revit Architecture, linked to an external database of sustainable materials and LEED information, designed to automate LEED point calculation and cost estimation.

Up to 3000 design families (RFA/RVT files) collected from Smart BIM library, suppliers' web pages, and published data, arranged by Masterformat WBS divisions, with associated LEED points and assembly codes.
Project name, address, owner, architect, estimator, number of stories, total area, total estimated cost, cost per square foot, date.

measures.details: Automatically calculated by the model based on selected sustainable materials/components and LEED-NC criteria.
Automatically calculated by the model based on building size, membership status (CaGBC), and selected certification type.
Calculated by a plug-in using Google Maps API based on postal codes, to determine eligibility for regional materials credits.
Qualitative claim of minimizing user input and increasing calculation efficiency.

data_collection_methods: Database compilation from Smart BIM library, supplier webpages, published data; user input for project information; automated calculation by BIM plug-in.
analysis_methods: Automated calculation and data retrieval via BIM plug-in linked to external database.

findings.antecedent: Use of the integrated BIM-LEED model (plug-in) at the conceptual design stage for a residential complex.
findings.quote: it was found that the total points the case building can earn for floors, roof, walls, doors and windows is 47 points, which shows that this building has a potential to be gold certified if it is registered for a LEED certificate.

findings.antecedent: Use of the integrated BIM-LEED model (plug-in) at the conceptual design stage for a residential complex.
findings.consequent: Estimated total soft cost for LEED registration and certification.
findings.quote: Fig. 9 shows the cost for registration, certification and total soft cost of the project as $315,814.

findings.antecedent: Automation of LEED point identification and cost estimation using the integrated BIM-LEED model.
findings.quote: Automating the process of identifying the potential number of LEED points... and estimating the associated costs will minimize users' input and will increase the calculations efficiency.

limitations: The model does not include all LEED products; it includes only LEED-NC.
The LEED credit accumulating plug-in only focused on Energy and Atmosphere (EA) and Materials and Resources (MR) credits.
The model does not incorporate the cost analysis for each point depending on the materials and systems used, besides the project size and cost.
The study looked only at the integration of BIM and sustainability from the LEED perspective, and only one LEED rating system (LEED-NC) was analyzed.
The results were limited to LEED instead of the general framework of sustainability.
future_research: Improving and enhancing the model to include all listed shortcomings.
